_comment: Scope name -> CSS class, for rendering TJSON on a web page. See
docs/web-highlighting.md. Kept as data rather than prose because
tests/scopes.js checks it against every scope the grammar actually emits,
so it cannot quietly fall behind the grammar the way a hand-written table
would.
Matching is by prefix and the list is ORDERED: take the first entry whose
prefix the scope equals or starts with (followed by a dot). Order matters in
three places -- .begin.bare must beat .definition.string, .multiline-margin
must beat .definition.string, and .separator.table must beat .separator.
`invalid` lands on the character that is in the wrong place, never on the
whitespace in front of it -- themes style `invalid` as a foreground colour
and an italic and never as a background, so on whitespace it renders as
nothing. YAML's `invalid.illegal.expected-indentation` follows the same
rule: the fault goes on the `-`, `?` or `|`, and the spaces beside it stay
ordinary indentation.
Walk a token's scopes from innermost to outermost and take the first hit;
the innermost scope is the most specific thing known about that text. A
scope listed under `unstyled` ends the walk instead of being skipped: it
says the text is deliberately not coloured, and reaching past it would
paint the indent in front of a fold marker with the colour of the string
that fold is continuing.
Deliberately given no class. `meta.*` marks a region rather than a token
and colouring it would paint whole lines. The indent is whitespace: it
carries structure, but there is nothing to see.
